item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Thu Oct 1 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Thu Oct 1 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Thu Oct 1 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Early Birds - — Thu Oct 1, 9:00 AM — Bryan Park Parking Lot
item.description:
See the new club calendar at bloomingtonbicycleclub.org for current rides.This group emphasizes earlier, moderate-paced rides with routes planned in advance and posted on the ride calendar. This is a no drop ride, but not a beginner's ride. Expect an overall average moving speed of 12 - 15 mph. Distances vary from 20 to a little over 30 miles. item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Thu Oct 1, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. item.title: Daniel Luis Martinez: The Blueprint | Exhibition — Fri Oct 2 — The Contemporary Art Museum of Indianapolis
item.description: Opening reception: Friday, October 2, 2026, 6–10pm Exhibition on view: October 2–December 18, 2026 For this exhibition, the blueprint is used as both a representational and conceptual departure point. Daniel Luis Martinez uses cyanotype printmaking and mixed-media drawing techniques as a generative process to imagine a speculative home on the CAMi campus. The hybrid drawings and prints featured in the exhibition explore the tactile middle-ground of the blueprint as a creative endeavor. The series employs orthographic conventions typical of architectural drawing sets, though not as precise instructions for building. Rather, a layered and loose approach expresses ideas of home as an architectonic language. Daniel Luis Martinez is a registered architect, educator, and co-founder of the multi-disciplinary design studio LAA Office, which explores the intersection of landscape, art, and architecture. His research and creative work investigate the potential of public art to generate alter

item.title: Kevin & Dianne Brown Students & Alumni Networking Dinner — Fri Oct 2, 5:00 PM — Neal-Marshall Black Culture Center275 N Eagleson Ave. Bloomington
item.description: Keynote Speaker: Kenneth L. Parker '97 — Kenneth L. Parker (https://www.taftlaw.com/people/kenneth-parker/) is a partner at Taft in Cincinnati, where he focuses his practice on compliance, investigations, white collar defense, and commercial litigation. Before joining Taft, Parker spent more than 25 years with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Ohio, including serving as the presidentially appointed U.S. Attorney from 2021 to 2025. During his tenure, he oversaw a wide range of criminal and civil matters involving public corruption, fraud, national security, cybercrime, civil rights, and other significant legal issues. A 1997 graduate of the Indiana University Maurer School of Law, Parker brings extensive experience in federal law enforcement and the legal profession to this year's Maurer Law community gathering.Event Schedule5 p.m. — Welcome Reception5:45 p.m. — Welcome & Introductions6 p.m. — Keynote Address6:30 p.m. — Dinner7:35 p.m. — Dessert & Alumni Reflection

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Tue Oct 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Tue Oct 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Tue Oct 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. item.title: Careers in NYC! | A Well-Advised Lunch with Jessie Bittner and Grace Lecky — Thu Oct 8, 12:00 PM — MERRILL HALL (MUSIC) / MUSIC
item.description:
Students, Sign Up Here > Jessie and Grace have forged distinctive, multifaceted careers in the performing arts and music industries. Jessie is a NYC-based singer, actor, multi-instrumentalist, music director, educator, and songwriter. She currently serves as Assistant Music Director and violinist for the national tour of the Tony Award-winning musical Hadestown, while maintaining an active career as a performer, teacher, and independent artist. After moving to New York, Grace joined the team at the legendary Power Station at BerkleeNYC while developing her own career as a songwriter, performer, producer, and audio professional. Together, Jessie and Grace will offer valuable perspectives on how to build networks and creative communities, balance multiple professional identities, and create sustainable careers in one of the world's most competitive cultural centers.
Source: IU Jacobs School of Music
